title: Arrakis: How To Build An AI Sandbox From Scratch - Abhishek Bhardwaj, OpenAI
talk_summary: Abhishek Bhardwaj explains how to build Arrakis, an open-source self-hosted AI sandbox using microVMs (Cloud Hypervisor) for secure code execution and computer use, covering Linux sandboxing tradeoffs, overlay filesystems, networking, and snapshot/restore. The core practical value is the snapshot/restore mechanism for agent backtracking and the microVM isolation model for untrusted agent code.

takeaways.what_they_do: Pause the VM, dump guest memory plus the writable overlay layer, then resume; agents restore a last-known-good checkpoint instead of restarting a failed multi-step workflow from scratch.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you should be able to backtrack to the last good checkpoint, replan and try again
takeaways.numbers: snapshots in single-digit seconds; boot <7s, targeting <1s

takeaways.technique: MicroVM isolation for untrusted agent code
takeaways.what_they_do: Run agent-generated code in microVMs (Cloud Hypervisor/Firecracker) with separate guest kernel instead of containers sharing the host kernel, reducing attack surface for multi-tenant untrusted code.

takeaways.technique: Overlay FS with shared read-only base + per-sandbox writable layer
takeaways.what_they_do: Share a read-only root filesystem across sandboxes and give each its own writable overlay layer; only persist the writable layer on snapshot.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every sandbox gets its own like readrite layer ... when we snapshot a sandbox we also persist or back up just the read write layer

takeaways.technique: Pre-baked tooling image (Chrome, Node, Python) to avoid runtime installs
takeaways.what_they_do: Base sandbox image ships standard packages, Chrome, Node/npm, Python so agents are productive without installing at runtime.
Because snapshots are cheap, agents can branch from a checkpoint and explore multiple execution paths in parallel, then keep the best.
takeaways.evidence_quote: at scale getting more reliable results by exploring multiple paths uh in parallel
